summary: Technical sync between Redwood (AE+SE) and NovaEdge to align on reference architecture for marketplace listing and joint solution. Discussed marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture components (VPC, KMS, private control plane), security/RBAC considerations, deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), and next steps for pilot and documentation. Agreed action items and timelines.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We wanted to run through the ref-arch and the marketplace checklist, make sure the NovaEdge side is comfortable with the flow.
[00:12] Daniel Park: Yep, thanks Maya. We have Lina and Arjun on too. The main ask is: can we list Redwood-backed offering in the NovaEdge marketplace and have a clear private deployment path—like reference arch we can hand to customers.
[00:30] Liam O'Connor: Cool, thanks. Quick agenda: 1) Reference architecture diagram and IaC, 2) marketplace listing requirements, 3) security/compliance Qs, 4) pilot plan.
[00:45] Sara Martinez: On the marketplace side, our product ops needs an AMI/container spec, a quickstart, and a blurb about SSO and network connectivity. Any constraints on image sizes or runtime?
[01:05] Maya Chen: For hosted listing we usually provide a connector config and a guided flow. For NovaEdge marketplace, we'll need to know whether you're doing a managed listing (we're the vendor) or marketplace as a launchpad for customer self-deploy.
[01:25] Daniel Park: We're looking at two models: 1) managed integration where Redwood manages inference for customers via our marketplace purchase; 2) customer-managed deploy using the ref-arch on customer infra.
[01:40] Liam O'Connor: That maps well. For managed we need SLA inputs and capacity reservation details. For customer-managed we provide Terraform modules, ref-arch diagrams, network/port lists, and KMS integration notes.
[02:05] Lina Gomez: Can you clarify KMS flow? Our security folks want to ensure keys never leave our control for private deployments.
[02:20] Liam O'Connor: Absolutely — for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM. The control plane can be private; the inference engines run in your V P C with a customer K M S key. There's also an option for envelope encryption if you want double wrap.
[02:40] Arjun Patel: Envelope wrapping sounds good. I noticed in past docs some references to K V cache — is that cached on the host or managed by Redwood? spelling in notes said 'K V cache' which confused some folks.
[03:00] Maya Chen: Sorry, transcription mix there sometimes — KV cache is the key-value attention cache for model state. In hosted mode we manage cache; in private/dedicated, the cache lives on your nodes and we surface controls for eviction and persistence.
[03:20] Sara Martinez: For marketplace listing we need a short doc describing supported instance types and expected L A T E N C Y at token sizes. Do you have a baseline we can reference?
[03:35] Liam O'Connor: Yes, I'll upload a baseline spreadsheet — typical p3/p4 equivalents, batch sizes, and latency at 512/1024 tokens. Note that quantization and batching change numbers a lot. We'll include a recommended profile for NovaEdge customers.
[04:00] Daniel Park: On the ref-arch diagram, can we show both flows: a) managed Redwood inference via NovaEdge entitlements and b) customer-self-deploy with IaC? We want to be explicit about where logs and telemetry land.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Makes sense, we'll produce two diagrams. For telemetry we usually include option to route logs to customer SIEM via syslog or cloud logging. For managed service we provide audit logs and can ship to your logging endpoint via a pull/export.
[04:40] Arjun Patel: Audit logs and RBAC are big for us. Do you integrate with S S O and SAML or only token-based access?
[04:55] Liam O'Connor: Redwood supports SAML/SSO for the control plane, and tokenized API keys for service-to-service. For enterprise private deployments we integrate with your identity provider and can map roles to RBAC. We'll document the mapping in the ref-arch.
[05:10] Lina Gomez: Any gotchas for VPC peering vs PrivateLink? Customers ask about NAT and egress charges.
[05:25] Maya Chen: Right — PrivateLink is recommended for minimal egress; VPC peering is fine but you end up with network pathing and potential egress. We'll document both options and cost tradeoffs.
[05:40] Sara Martinez: Marketplace copy: we need a one-paragraph summary and a bulleted feature list. Also legal wants a data flow diagram for review.
[05:55] Daniel Park: On legal, we also need a model data residency statement — if customer data is processed in Redwood-hosted flow how long is data retained?
[06:10] Liam O'Connor: Good point. For hosted we have configurable retention; default is 30 days for logs and model caching ephemeral, but we can sign specific retention in contracts. For Dedicated and Private deployments, data stays in-customer environment. We'll include that language in the draft listing.
[06:30] Arjun Patel: What about SOC2 and ISO? We need copies for procurement.
[06:40] Maya Chen: We can share SOC2 attestation and the security datasheet. Also provide our K M S integration guide and network checklist. I'll drop links in the follow-up.
[06:55] Lina Gomez: Are there any known performance regressions when using quantized models in a private deployment? We need to call that out in the ref-arch.
[07:10] Liam O'Connor: Quantization often increases throughput and reduces memory but can affect quality for some models. We'll include a section about recommended quant profiles per model family and a note about doing regression tests with your eval sets. We also recommend continuous evals as part of the ref-arch.
[07:40] Daniel Park: For the marketplace listing test, we want a staging flow. Could Redwood host a short trial instance for our QA team?
[07:55] Maya Chen: Yes, we can spin up a short-lived staging instance in Redwood's hosted environment and share access, or we can assist with a local deploy to NovaEdge staging. Which do you prefer?
[08:12] Sara Martinez: Staging hosted by Redwood would be faster for QA but procurement may prefer full customer-managed test. We'll start with Redwood-hosted demo for feature validation then move to staging deploy.
[08:30] Liam O'Connor: OK we'll plan for a hosted staging first. I'll add steps for provisioning and access controls.
[08:42] Arjun Patel: One more on encryption — can we get a short note on audit trail for key rotations? We rotate keys every 90 days internally.
[08:55] Maya Chen: We support key rotation; for customer-managed KMS you control rotations. For managed KMS we provide rotation logs and will surface events in audit logs. We'll add language and sample event schema.
[09:12] Daniel Park: Logistics: who owns the marketplace listing copy and legal review?
[09:25] Maya Chen: Redwood can draft the initial copy and the ref-arch. NovaEdge will review and send redlines; legal/ops alignment can happen once draft is in.
[09:40] Lina Gomez: Timeline question: can we get the draft ref-arch and Terraform in five days?
[09:50] Maya Chen: Yes, we can aim for 2026-05-25. Liam will attach the performance baseline in the next two business days.
[10:05] Liam O'Connor: I'll also include sample IaC snippets — Terraform modules for VPC, KMS integration, and an example helm chart snippet for on-prem deploys. Note: some customers use Helm with custom init containers to mount K M S credentials.
[10:30] Sara Martinez: On the marketplace side we need to confirm billing flows — purchase triggers entitlement in NovaEdge, does Redwood surface usage to NovaEdge for revenue share?
[10:45] Maya Chen: We'll need to sync with partnerships ops, but in past integrations we support metered usage reports (CSV/API) and can push usage events to partner endpoints. We'll include a spec for that in the joint doc.
[11:05] Daniel Park: Any blockers you see from Redwood side?
[11:15] Liam O'Connor: Nothing immediate — we just need account info for marketplace sandbox and NovaEdge to confirm whether images must be signed or any special packaging.
[11:30] Arjun Patel: Regarding packaging, NovaEdge requires a signed manifest for images. Are you able to support that?
[11:40] Maya Chen: Yes, we have signed image pipelines and can produce signed manifests for the listing. We'll include sample signatures.
[11:55] Lina Gomez: For joint solutions marketing, we should include a reference architecture with callouts for observability — console dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks.
[12:10] Liam O'Connor: We'll annotate those in the diagram — show where tracing and cost logs live, and include pointers to Redwood Console features like route-level latency breakdowns.
[12:30] Sara Martinez: Anything else on security posture?
[12:40] Arjun Patel: Would like a quick runbook for incident response — who to call and how we exchange creds safely.
[12:55] Maya Chen: We'll add a runbook appendix: escalation contacts, rotation steps, and a secure channel for temporary creds — recommend ephemeral tokens via Vault or OIDC where possible.
[13:15] Daniel Park: Great. Let's recap actions.
[13:20] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share draft ref-arch, Terraform, IaC snippets, performance baseline, SOC2/security docs; NovaEdge to provide sandbox account details, signed image requirements, and compliance questions. We'll target the dates in the follow-up.
[13:40] Sara Martinez: Thanks, that works.
[13:45] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with links and the draft by Tuesday.
[13:52] [END OF RECORDING]
notes: References: ref-arch draft (will be shared), performance-baseline.xlsx (to be uploaded), marketplace-checklist.docx (NovaEdge format). Participants agreed on dual-flow ref-arch (managed vs customer-managed). Key security items: customer-managed KMS, SOC2 docs, RBAC mapping, signed image manifests.
closing_summary: Agreement to produce two reference architecture variants, provide IaC and performance baselines, and run a hosted staging test. Action owners and dates captured. Next sync to review drafts and legal redlines.
